Keep the same minimal shape as the workspace baseline in `projects/template/likec4.config.json`: `$schema`, `name`, `title`, `include.paths`, and `imageAliases`. From `projects/payments`, shared specs should be referenced with `../shared`, and shared icons should keep `"@": "../shared/images/"`. Use paths relative to the project folder, not workspace-root or absolute paths.

Safe minimal file: {"$schema":"https://likec4.dev/schemas/config.json","name":"payments","title":"Payments Architecture","include":{"paths":["../shared"]},"imageAliases":{"@":"../shared/images/"}}

Split it progressively, not as a one-shot rewrite. First move elements and relationships into `system-model.c4`, then put the index plus all C1/C2/C3 views into `system-views.c4`. That gives you the clean baseline with the smallest useful split: `likec4.config.json`, `system-model.c4`, and `system-views.c4`.

Only extract more files when the topic is big enough to deserve it: put dynamic flows in `system-sequences.c4` under `Use Cases`, deployment nodes and `instanceOf` in `deployment.c4` with deployment views in `deployment-views.c4`, and operational topology in `operations.c4` with operations views in `operations-views.c4`. Keep C1/C2/C3 in `system-views.c4`, and use the view folders `C1`, `C2`, `C3`, `Use Cases`, `Deployment`, and `Operations` rather than scattering views across mixed files.

Treat this as a targeted config edit, not a full model reorganization. Keep the existing `include.paths` entries exactly as they are and append the new source instead of replacing the array, for example `['../shared', '../platform-shared', '../new-common-source']`.

Order matters because it preserves current resolution behavior: keeping `../shared` first and `../platform-shared` second minimizes surprises for anything already resolving from those sources, so add the new path after them unless you intentionally want different precedence. Also keep `imageAliases` intact—especially the shared `"@": "../shared/images/"` mapping—so existing icons keep working. Stay with relative paths only; avoid absolute paths.

Not by itself. This skill is the right one for the project-local part—editing each `likec4.config.json`, preserving `include.paths`, and keeping image aliases such as `"@": "../shared/images/"` correct with relative paths like `../shared`.

But adding a second LikeC4 project is also a workspace-organization decision, so combine this with `organize-multi-project` for the overall structure and project boundaries. In short: use `organize-multi-project` for the workspace layout, then use this skill for the per-project config details.

Keep this as a surgical config change. In `include.paths`, preserve `../shared` and append `../platform-shared` after it: `['../shared', '../platform-shared']`. That order should be explicit because include order affects resolution; keeping `../shared` first preserves current behavior, and you should only reverse the order if you intentionally want `../platform-shared` to take precedence.

For `imageAliases`, do not reuse the same alias for both sources. Keep the existing shared alias as `"@": "../shared/images/"` so current icons do not break, and add a distinct alias for platform images, for example `"@platform": "../platform-shared/images/"`. That avoids alias collisions instead of blindly merging two sources under the same key, and it keeps all paths relative to `projects/payments`.
